title: Gate the standard's fixtures: 12 stated outcomes in spec section 12 are run by no gate
body:
## Summary
The spec lists what each schema fixture must do (4 fail, 2 pass, 5 healths and a rollup in valid-applies-when), but no gate runs any of it, so a schema or evaluator change can break every stated outcome with all gates green.

## Description
docs/standard/app-structure-v3.md:657-667 states: valid-map.json (+ events) and valid-applies-when.json validate; invalid-stage, invalid-lens-id, invalid-two-operators and invalid-core-field fail, each for a named reason; valid-applies-when reads book-a-class bad, loyalty-points na (applies_when outranks an override in force), spot-selection watch (stored stage ignored), class-packs na, virtual-classes unmeasured, rollup bad. docs/standard/personas-adoption.md:93 and :160 make the Personas port's acceptance depend on the same outcomes. The overlay gates are typecheck, check:lens-health (Kettle sample, built-ins only) and validate:structure over the Kettle map - none opens docs/standard/schema/fixtures/. Today all 12 outcomes hold (probed by hand this round), which is exactly when an instrument is cheapest to seed. Fixed looks like: scripts/check-standard-fixtures.mjs that runs validate-structure on each fixture and asserts exit code plus the expected error substring, and evaluates valid-applies-when through src/lib/standard/health.ts (lensHealth with feature context, rollupHealth), exiting 1 on any mismatch; wired as an npm script and an overlay gate when docs/standard or src/lib/standard change.

## Flow
- write scripts/check-standard-fixtures.mjs from the expectations in spec section 12 (start from scratchpad probe-aw.mjs)
- run it on the base tree: 12 of 12 pass
- seed: flip invalid-stage.json's stage to 'live' -> the check exits 1; flip the override's `until` precedence in health.ts lensHealth (move step 5 above step 4) -> loyalty-points reads bad, check exits 1; revert both
- add `check:standard-fixtures` to package.json (director) and to the overlay's gate list

## Expected impact
A change to a schema, the validator or the evaluator that breaks a published fixture outcome goes red at the change instead of in the Personas port. Could break nothing: the script only reads.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every fixture outcome the spec states is gated
Before: 0 of 12 stated outcomes run by any gate (overlay gates read no file under docs/standard/schema/fixtures)
After: 12 of 12 asserted by the new check, each seeded red once
Method: probe - the 12 outcomes were reproduced by hand this round (validate-structure exit codes and error text per fixture; lensHealth/rollupHealth over valid-applies-when); the gate itself is not built because scripts/ and package.json are outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
node scripts/validate-structure.mjs <fixture>: invalid-core-field 1, invalid-lens-id 1, invalid-stage 1, invalid-two-operators 1, valid-applies-when 0, valid-map 0 (+events 0)
errors: 'a field can bind only to the core feature fields ... (got "owner")'; 'a custom lens (source "project") needs a reverse-DNS id'; 'must be one of: idea, ... (got "shipped")'; 'condition leaf on "openFindings" has 2 operators (gt, lt)'
valid-applies-when via health.ts: book-a-class bad, loyalty-points na, spot-selection watch, class-packs na, virtual-classes unmeasured, rollup bad
git grep 'schema/fixtures' -- scripts package.json .claude/scan-sweep/config.md -> no hits
instrument: scripts/check-standard-fixtures.mjs itself (S): 12 assertions; control seeded red twice (fixture flip, precedence swap). Scratch starting points: scratchpad/probe-aw.mjs, scratchpad/optimize/standard/probe-example.mjs

title: Read the built-in lens list from catalog.ts in the two gate scripts
body:
## Summary
scripts/validate-structure.mjs:20 and scripts/check-builtin-health.ts:22-23 each re-list the six built-in lens ids and read their files by path; since 7d0cab6 Node can import src/lib/standard/catalog.ts, which is the list.

## Description
The built-in ids were written in four places; a867c10 removed the dead one and 7d0cab6 made catalog.ts (BUILTIN_LENSES) loadable under Node type stripping, so the two scripts were the only reason left for re-listing. A seventh built-in, a rename, or a reorder now needs three coordinated edits (catalog.ts imports, validate-structure BUILTIN, check-builtin-health IDS), and validate-structure's no-arg run would silently skip a new built-in the catalog ships. Fixed: check-builtin-health imports BUILTIN_LENSES; validate-structure's no-arg mode derives its file list from the catalog ids (it is .mjs: import the .ts module under type stripping, or read the ids from the lens schema's builtinLensId enum, which is already the normative list - lens-manifest-1.schema.json:35).

## Flow
- check-builtin-health.ts: replace IDS + per-file read with `import { BUILTIN_LENSES } from '../src/lib/standard/catalog.ts'`
- validate-structure.mjs: derive BUILTIN from lensSchema.$defs.builtinLensId.enum (no TS import needed) and keep the id-vs-filename check
- re-run both: same output as base
- seed: add a seventh id to the schema enum -> no-arg validate fails on the missing file (today it would not notice)

## Expected impact
One place to add or rename a built-in lens per consumer class (code: catalog.ts; tools: the schema enum). Could break: the no-arg validator's file list if the enum and files diverge - which is the point.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - fewer hand lists of one fact
Before: 3 hand lists of the built-in ids (catalog.ts imports, validate-structure.mjs:20, check-builtin-health.ts:22)
After: 1 hand list per authority (catalog.ts for code, schema enum for tools), scripts derived; outputs byte-identical
Method: probe - counted the lists by grep; Node import of catalog.ts verified (5/5 modules load); edit not made because scripts/ is outside this context's paths (the tooling round owns it this wave)
Result: better
Gate: none
trigger: out-of-scope (scripts/ - tooling context, in flight this wave)
instrument: byte-diff of `node scripts/validate-structure.mjs` and `node scripts/check-builtin-health.ts` output, base vs arm; plus the seeded seventh schema id going red on the arm only

title: A corrupt or locked scan store reads as 'No scan store yet' on the client
standard: error-handling (registry software-engineering: 'The error door: every failure reaches somewhere', 'The dominant defect is silence')
body:
## Summary
When scan.db exists but cannot be read, the stream answers an empty snapshot and the client shows the 'no store yet' state instead of an error.

## Description
src/app/api/products/[slug]/stream/route.ts:53 sends `emptyScan()` whenever `connect()` fails, and connect() fails both when the file is absent (correct: 'missing') and when it exists but readSnapshot throws (corrupt file, schema mid-migration, lock past the busy timeout). src/lib/scan/client.ts:76-81 then derives `hasStore = false` from the empty scan and reads `missing`. The server now logs it once (1b3d2f6) but the person at the screen is told the skill has not run. Fixed looks like: a distinct SSE `event: error` ({ message }) when the file exists and cannot be read, StreamEvent gains 'error', and useLiveProduct sets status 'error' with the text until the next good snapshot.

## Flow
- write garbage to <root>/.ai/lens-scan/scan.db -> open ?product=<slug>
- route: fs.existsSync true -> openRead ok -> readSnapshot throws -> catch -> send('snapshot', emptyScan())
- client: snapshot empty -> hasStore false -> status 'missing' -> pill 'No scan store'
- fix, in build order: StreamEvent 'error' in types.ts; route sends it when the file exists and connect failed (once per message); client listener sets status 'error'; docs/blueprint-ui.md SSE semantics line

## Expected impact
An operator whose store broke sees 'error: file is not a database' instead of being sent to run the skill again. Could break: a client that treats unknown SSE events as fatal (EventSource ignores unnamed listeners, so none in-tree).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a store that exists but cannot be read is shown as an error, not as absent
Before: stream probe (route handler over a corrupt scan.db, 3.5 s): 1 event to the client, an empty snapshot; client state 'missing'
After: predicted 1 `error` event carrying 'file is not a database', client state 'error' - not taken
Method: simulation - the route side is probed (scratch probe below); the client state needs a hook/EventSource harness this round did not build, and the change is an in-tree contract (StreamEvent) across types, route, client and a doc outside this context
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
src/app/api/products/[slug]/stream/route.ts:41-53 (connect -> catch -> false -> send('snapshot', emptyScan()))
src/lib/scan/client.ts:76-81 (if (!isEmpty(scan)) hasStore = true; status shown() -> 'missing')
probe output: events to client: ["snapshot {\"runs\":[],...}"]  server warnings: 1 ['[bp] stream x (...scan.db): file is not a database']
instrument: scratchpad/optimize/model-and-data/probe/stream-probe.mts (node --experimental-transform-types, resolve hooks in hooks.mjs, BP_ROOT=<worktree>): runs the stream GET over a corrupt store and lists the SSE events; extend it to assert an `error` event, plus a client check that feeds useLiveProduct's listeners (or swaps EventSource) and asserts status 'error'. Contract letters: (a) consumers = client.ts only (grep StreamEvent / addEventListener), (c) the probe pins 'error' and forbids an empty snapshot for an existing unreadable file

title: @types/node 26 types a Node 24 runtime
body:
## Summary
package.json pins @types/node ^26.6.4 while the runtime here is Node v24.12.0, so tsc accepts Node 26 APIs that do not exist where the store code runs.

## Description
src/lib/scan/store.server.ts:6 and docs/blueprint-ui.md:271 both state node:sqlite is a Node 24 builtin (experimental). The type package is two majors ahead (`npm outdated`: @types/node 26.6.4 -> 26.6.5), so a call to a DatabaseSync option or fs API added in 25/26 typechecks and fails at runtime on 24. Fixed looks like @types/node matching the runtime major (^24) or an `engines.node` that says 26, whichever the operator intends; package.json has no `engines` field today.

## Flow
- install @types/node@24 in a worktree -> npm run typecheck -> count errors (each one is a 25/26-only API in use, or a types drift)
- if 0 errors: pin ^24 (and add engines >=24 <25 if the operator wants it)

## Expected impact
A Node-26-only call is caught by typecheck instead of at request time. Could break: nothing at runtime; typecheck may surface errors that were hidden.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - types match the runtime that executes the code
Before: @types/node major 26 vs runtime 24.12.0; APIs-beyond-24 in use: unknown
After: not taken - needs a version change in package.json/package-lock.json (director-owned, network install)
Method: simulation - the instrument is a typecheck under @types/node@24, which needs an install this round must not make
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: package.json devDependencies "@types/node": "^26.6.4"; node --version -> v24.12.0; no "engines" key; src/lib/scan/store.server.ts:6 'node:sqlite is a Node builtin (experimental on 24)'
instrument: in a worktree: npm i -D @types/node@24 && npm run typecheck - the error count is the figure (0 -> pin is free; N -> each is a Node 25/26 API in use)

title: Gate theme-token completeness and var() resolution in a node check
standard: software-engineering/design-tokens (theming is token redefinition: completeness is per-theme and provable; token-enforcement)
body:
## Summary
Nothing checks that the light and dark themes define the same tokens, or that every var(--x) in the app resolves; parity holds today (37/37) only by hand.

## Description
src/app/globals.css:5-90 defines the dark and light token sets; src/engine/theme.ts:82 reads them back with hard-coded dark fallbacks, so a token missing from the light block silently renders dark-theme colours on the canvas and nothing on the DOM. No gate reads globals.css: `npm run typecheck` and `check:lens-health` cannot see CSS. The design-tokens golden path says completeness must be provable per theme and the floor checked by a gate that reads the actual theme definitions. Fixed = a scripts/check-tokens.mjs that parses both theme blocks, fails on any name defined in one and not the other, and fails on any var(--x) or getPropertyValue('--x') in src/ that resolves nowhere (allow-list: --font-* from next/font, --cx/--sw/--rw/--p set inline, with the allow-list derived from a grep for style.setProperty / style={{'--x'}} rather than hand-kept).

## Flow
- write scripts/check-tokens.mjs (plain node, no deps)
- seed red: delete --poche from the light block, run, expect exit 1 naming --poche; delete a var() target, expect exit 1
- restore, run green (expect 37/37, 0 unresolved)
- wire as npm run check:tokens (package.json is director-owned) and add it to the overlay's always-gates

## Expected impact
A theme regression (a token added to dark only) fails at commit instead of shipping a canvas painted with dark fallbacks in light mode. Could break: nothing at runtime; a false red if the allow-list is hand-kept and goes stale.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - theme completeness and token resolution are enforced, not hoped
Before: 0 gates read globals.css; probe this round: 37/37 parity, 7 names resolved outside globals (3 by next/font, 4 set inline), all legitimate, 0 seeded violations ever caught
After: a gate that goes red on a seeded missing light token and a seeded unresolved var(), green on the tree
Method: experiment - the parity/resolution script ran this round from scratch (tokcheck); it cannot land because scripts/ and package.json are outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: scratch probe output: dark 38 light 38 dark-only [] light-only []; used 57; unresolved outside globals: --font-sans/--font-mono/--font-hand (next/font), --cx, --sw (blueprint.css, set inline), --rw (timeline.css), --p (shaped/styles.css); src/engine/theme.ts:82 v = getPropertyValue(n).trim() || fallback
instrument: scripts/check-tokens.mjs: parse the two :root blocks of src/app/globals.css, diff the name sets, scan src/ for var(--x)/getPropertyValue('--x') and for inline setters; seed control red by deleting --poche from the light block

title: Correct the route table in docs/blueprint-ui.md: '/' is the blueprint, '/variants' the index
standard: software-engineering/docs-sync (named-duplication-points: a restated fact changed in one document and the other still carries the old value)
body:
## Summary
The UI contract says '/' is the variant index and the blueprint lives at /v/[variant]; since the owner adopted subtle, '/' renders the blueprint and the index moved to /variants.

## Description
docs/blueprint-ui.md:118 (`src/app/ routes (App Router). '/' = variant index; '/v/[variant]' = the blueprint`) and :212-213 (`plus '/' (an index with the three cards and the theme toggle)`) contradict src/app/page.tsx:9-11 (`BlueprintApp variantId="subtle"`, comment: the three prototypes stay at /variants) and README.md's route table, which is right. The doc is the file the brief tells every builder to read first, so a builder reading it will look for the blueprint in the wrong route. Fixed = both lines say '/' = the blueprint (subtle), '/variants' = the index, '/v/[variant]' = one variant.

## Flow
- edit docs/blueprint-ui.md:118 and :212-213
- re-check: grep the doc for "'/'" claims and compare each with src/app/**/page.tsx

## Expected impact
Builders and reviewers find the right route. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the contract's route claims match the routes
Before: 2 of 2 route claims about '/' false (blueprint-ui.md:118, :212)
After: 0 of 2 false
Method: probe - the claims were read against src/app/page.tsx and src/app/variants/page.tsx; not built because docs/ is outside this context's paths (veto 1)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
docs/blueprint-ui.md:118  src/app/ routes (App Router). '/' = variant index; '/v/[variant]' = the blueprint
docs/blueprint-ui.md:212  These are routes /v/subtle, /v/shaped and /v/bold, plus / (an index with the three cards and the theme toggle)
src/app/page.tsx:9-11  // The owner adopted the subtle lens expression (2026-10-09); the three prototypes stay at /variants. ... return <BlueprintApp variantId="subtle" />
README.md route table: / = the blueprint, /variants = the three expressions
instrument: grep docs/blueprint-ui.md for route claims and diff against src/app/**/page.tsx (2 false -> 0)

title: Stop next dev from dirtying the tree (next-env.d.ts rewrite, generated AGENTS.md)
standard: software-engineering/build-economics (judged on repo conventions: the overlay's never-touch list exists because of this)
body:
## Summary
Every `next dev` run leaves two changes in a clean worktree: next-env.d.ts is rewritten to the dev types path and an untracked AGENTS.md is generated.

## Description
Next 16.4 writes `import "./.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts"` into next-env.d.ts under dev and `./.next/types/...` under build, so the tracked file flips between the two on every switch; it also prints 'Generated AGENTS.md for AI agents. Set agentRules: false in next.config to disable.' and writes AGENTS.md at the repo root. Each sweep agent has to be told never to stage them (the overlay's never-touch list), and every parallel worktree that runs a dev server shows them as litter. Fixed = `agentRules: false` in next.config.ts and next-env.d.ts gitignored (Next 16 regenerates it on every dev/build/typecheck), so a dev run leaves `git status --porcelain` empty.

## Flow
- add agentRules: false to next.config.ts
- git rm --cached next-env.d.ts; add it to .gitignore
- check that `npm run typecheck` still passes on a fresh clone (tsc needs next-env.d.ts: confirm `next typegen` or the build creates it, else keep it tracked and only take the AGENTS.md half)
- run next dev once, kill it, assert git status --porcelain is empty

## Expected impact
Sweep agents and humans stop seeing two phantom changes after every dev run. Could break: a fresh clone's typecheck if next-env.d.ts is not regenerated before tsc.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - dev runs leave the tree clean
Before: 2 paths dirtied by one next dev run on this worktree (M next-env.d.ts, ?? AGENTS.md), reproduced twice this round
After: predicted 0; not taken
Method: probe for Before only - next.config.ts, .gitignore and next-env.d.ts are outside this context's paths (veto 1), and next-env.d.ts is on the brief's never-touch list
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
dev log: '✓ Generated AGENTS.md for AI agents. Set `agentRules: false` in next.config to disable.'
git diff next-env.d.ts: -import "./.next/types/routes.d.ts"; +import "./.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts" (and root-params.d.ts)
git status --porcelain after one run: ' M next-env.d.ts', '?? AGENTS.md'
instrument: run next dev on a clean worktree, wait for the first GET / 200, kill it, count `git status --porcelain` lines (2 -> 0); plus `npm run typecheck` on a fresh clone

title: Raster the static layer without its 22% margin while the lens mix springs
standard: software-engineering/canvas-graph#render-budget (rung 3: a lens change should not repaint what it does not touch; rung 0: measure the selection-change case)
body:
## Summary
Every frame of a lens switch re-rasters the whole static plan at full margin (viewport + 22% each side, 2.07x the visible area), and at room/tile zoom that raster costs 39-51 ms per frame, so the 0.5 s tween runs at ~20-30 fps.

## Description
The static key includes mixV (src/engine/Engine.ts:299), so each tween frame is `stale` and src/engine/Engine.ts:339 calls StaticCache.render, which always covers the margin (src/engine/render/static-cache.ts:47, MARGIN=0.22 at :10). The margin only pays off for a later pan; during a tween the camera is still and the margin is pure raster area. Full raster cost (record + the flush Chrome defers to the first drawImage) per LOD at ?scale=4, 1920x1080 DPR1, dev server: home 18.7-19.1 ms, L-bld 20.8-22.3, L-blend 27.0-27.5, L-tiles 38.7-40.1, L-room 45.4-51.4, L-feat 21.6-21.9. On a tablet (820x1180 DPR2, 8.0 MP raster, the 12 MP cap never binds) the same rasters cost 27-59 ms (L-blend 58.9). Fix: StaticCache.render takes a margin argument; Engine passes 0 while `this.mix.moving`. The tween's last frame (animationComplete -> mixV++ with moving=false) rasters at full margin, so a pan after the switch is unaffected.

## Flow
- user switches General -> a lens at L-tiles/L-room zoom -> MixDriver onChange per weight -> mixV++ -> staticKey changes -> full-margin raster every frame -> 39-51 ms frames
- build: add `margin = MARGIN` parameter to StaticCache.render (static-cache.ts:44,47); pass `this.mix.moving ? 0 : undefined` at Engine.ts:342
- measure with tween.py (rAF deltas over General->lens->General) at four zooms on both arms, interleaved, plus a pan right after the tween (rasters during the pan must not rise)

## Expected impact
Anyone switching lenses zoomed in, most on DPR2 tablets: fewer dropped frames during the 0.5 s spring. Could break: a pan started mid-tween leaves the covered area at once and re-rasters on its first frame (one hitch where today there is none).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - lens-switch frames at tile/room zoom
Before: tween.py, subtle, dev server: L-room 57-59 frames in 2.4 s, p50 49.9-50 ms, p95 83.3; L-bld 80 frames p50 33.3
After: same instrument on a prototype (margin 0 while mix.moving, reverted): L-room 77-82 frames, p50 33.3, p95 50-66.7; L-bld 99-100 frames p50 16.7; home unchanged (63-67 frames)
Method: probe - prototype applied to Engine.ts + static-cache.ts in the worktree and reverted; Engine.ts belongs to engine-interaction (a sibling round), so it cannot land here; noisy machine (three sibling rounds), so the worker must interleave arms
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/engine/Engine.ts:299 staticKey includes this.mixV
src/engine/Engine.ts:125 MixDriver onChange -> this.mixV++
src/engine/Engine.ts:339-342 this.cache.render(c, key, FW, FH, RES, paint)
src/engine/render/static-cache.ts:10 MARGIN = 0.22; :47 mx = round(FW * MARGIN)
lodprobe full raster ms (desktop): 19.1 / 20.8 / 27.0 / 40.1 / 45.4 / 21.9 (home..L-feat); tablet 820x1180@2: 27.1 / 36.2 / 58.9 / 49.9 / 53.6 / 45.8
tween.py L-room before: frames 57-59, p50 49.9-50; prototype: frames 77-82, p50 33.3
instrument: C:/Users/mkdol/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-mkdol-dolla-bp/7315829e-d694-4a70-b7bd-57dc9b6786c5/scratchpad/optimize/canvas-render/tween.py (rAF deltas during General->lens->General at home, L-bld, L-tiles, L-room; BP_BASE=http://localhost:<port>) and lodprobe.py (per-LOD full raster ms; VW=820 VH=1180 DPR=2 for the tablet arm). Seed red: margin 0 on every raster must show a raster on the first pan frame after the tween.

title: Time the static raster where Chrome actually pays it, and measure every LOD
body:
## Summary
perf.lastRasterMs reports only the time spent issuing canvas calls; Chrome defers the 2D raster to the first drawImage of the cache, which is 3-4x the reported figure, and scripts/perf.py measures one gesture at one LOD path.

## Description
StaticCache.render times paint() alone (src/engine/render/static-cache.ts:45-61) and Engine copies it straight after render (src/engine/Engine.ts:343). The deferred raster lands in StaticCache.draw's drawImage (static-cache.ts:73): a CPU profile of 60 rasters at L-room put 58-60% of self time in drawImage. docs/perf.md:24-26 states the lens tween re-rasters "28-33 rasters of 3-4 ms each" from that counter; the real per-raster frame cost at L0 is ~19-21 ms and 45-51 ms at room zoom (dev server). scripts/perf.py:13-31 drives a wheel zoom + drag from home only, never the lens tween and never a fixed LOD. Fix: (1) Engine records lastRasterMs after the first cache.draw following a raster (or StaticCache times its first draw after render and Engine reads it after draw); (2) perf.py gains a per-LOD raster mode and a tween mode (the two probes below); (3) docs/perf.md re-measured on a production build.

## Flow
- run perf.py today -> lastRasterMs ~4-11 ms reported while E.draw with an invalidated cache takes 19-51 ms
- build: move the perf.lastRasterMs read after this.cache.draw (Engine.ts:343/351) and include the first draw's time; add `--lod` and `--tween` modes to scripts/perf.py from lodprobe.py/tween.py; re-measure docs/perf.md on `npm run build && npm start`

## Expected impact
Whoever tunes the canvas reads the real cost per level of detail instead of a quarter of it; the 60 fps claim in docs/perf.md gains the tween and per-LOD rows it lacks. Could break: nothing user-visible; perf.py output shape changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the counter and the perf script report the cost the user pays, at every LOD
Before: lodprobe, dev, 1920x1080: recorded vs full raster ms home 6.4 vs 19.1, L-bld 6.2 vs 20.8, L-tiles 8.7 vs 40.1, L-room 11.1 vs 45.4 (counter = 24-34% of the real cost); perf.py covers 1 gesture path, 0 of 6 fixed LODs, 0 tweens
After: counter within the noise of the full E.draw figure at each LOD; perf.py covers 6 of 6 LODs and the tween (instruments already written)
Method: probe - both figures taken on the real tree (E.cache.invalidate + E.draw timed vs perf.lastRasterMs); the fix needs Engine.ts, scripts/ and docs/ - none in this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/engine/render/static-cache.ts:45 t0 = performance.now(); :57 paint(...); :61 lastMs = performance.now() - t0
src/engine/Engine.ts:343 this.perf.lastRasterMs = this.cache.lastMs (before cache.draw at :351)
CPU profile (profile.py subtle 3 60): drawImage 2695 ms of 4610 ms self (58.5%), render() 1120 ms inclusive
docs/perf.md "28-33 rasters of 3-4 ms each"
lodprobe recMed vs fullMed: 6.4/19.1, 6.2/20.8, 5.3/27.0, 8.7/40.1, 11.1/45.4, 4.2/21.9
instrument: C:/Users/mkdol/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-mkdol-dolla-bp/7315829e-d694-4a70-b7bd-57dc9b6786c5/scratchpad/optimize/canvas-render/lodprobe.py (recMed = counter, fullMed = invalidated E.draw) and profile.py; seed red: the fixed counter must read <50% of fullMed if the flush timing is removed

title: A select-mode lasso stays drawn through a pinch (Engine.ts pinch start and end never clear this.lasso)
standard: software-engineering/canvas-graph (direct-manipulation: a gesture handed to another gesture leaves no provisional state behind)
body:
## Summary
On a touch device in select mode, a lasso started with one finger stays on screen, frozen, for the whole pinch that a second finger starts, and until the last finger lifts.

## Description
The pointerdown handler at src/engine/Engine.ts:846 turns a second pointer into a pinch and sets `this.drag = null`, but leaves `this.lasso` as the first finger last drew it. The pinch branch of pointermove returns before the lasso is touched, and the pinch branch of `end` (src/engine/Engine.ts:877 on HEAD, `if (this.pinch) { ...; return; }`) returns before the `this.lasso = null` further down. `drawLasso` (src/engine/render/dynamic.ts) paints `E.lasso` every frame, so a dashed selection box hangs over a plan that is zooming under it, and no target is set from it. Fixed: clear `this.lasso` where the pinch starts and on the pinch's end path.

## Flow
- tablet, press S (select mode) -> one finger drags > 5 px -> `this.lasso` is set and drawn
- a second finger touches -> pinch starts, `drag = null`, `lasso` unchanged
- pinch -> the plan zooms, the lasso box stays at its old screen position
- lift one finger -> the pinch branch returns early, lasso still set; lift the other -> cleared
- fix: `this.lasso = null` beside `this.drag = null` at pinch start, and in the pinch branch of `end`

## Expected impact
Tablet users in select mode stop seeing a stale selection box over a zooming plan. Nothing else reads `lasso` mid-pinch (lassoSelect runs only from a non-pinch pointerup), so nothing should break.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no lasso is drawn while a pinch is in progress
Before: walked: lasso non-null from pinch start until the last finger lifts (3 paths read: pointerdown, pointermove pinch branch, end pinch branch)
After: predicted null from the second finger's pointerdown
Method: simulation - the rung above needs a touch-capable browser; this worktree runs node gates on a node_modules junction, and next dev panics on it (npm ci + a dev server were outside this round's budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/engine/Engine.ts:846  if (this.ptrs.size === 2) { ...; this.pinch = {...}; this.drag = null; return; }   // lasso kept
src/engine/Engine.ts:877  if (this.pinch) { if (this.ptrs.size < 2) this.pinch = null; this.drag = null; return; }   // returns before the lasso reset
src/engine/Engine.ts:891  this.lasso = null; this.drag = null; ...
instrument: Playwright at 820x1180 with hasTouch on ?scale=1 after npm ci + next dev: press S, CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent one touchStart+touchMove (40 px), then a second touchStart and a touchMove spreading the two; read window.__bp.lasso during the pinch. Control: non-null on the base tree; arm B: null.

title: Declare the Python tool dependencies (playwright, Pillow) the shot and perf scripts import
body:
## Summary
Ten Python scripts import playwright or PIL, and no manifest in the repo declares either.

## Description
scripts/shots.py, scripts/perf.py and the six variant tools (src/variants/bold/shots.py, bold/perf.py, shaped/shots.py, shaped/perf_lens.py, subtle/tools/shots.py, subtle/tools/perf_lens.py) import playwright; src/variants/subtle/tools/crop.py and grid.py import PIL. There is no requirements.txt or pyproject.toml, and README.md names `python scripts/shots.py` without an install line, so a fresh machine learns the dependency from a ModuleNotFoundError. Fixed = a root requirements-tools.txt (playwright, Pillow) plus one README line (`pip install -r requirements-tools.txt && playwright install chromium`).

## Flow
- add requirements-tools.txt at the root with the two packages
- add the install line beside `python scripts/shots.py` in README.md
- verify: a fresh venv installs from it and `python -c 'import playwright, PIL'` passes

## Expected impact
A contributor or agent can run the screenshot and perf tools without guessing. Could break: nothing at runtime; the files are shared root files.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every third-party Python import is declared
Before: 2 third-party packages imported by 10 scripts, declared in 0 manifests
After: 2 of 2 declared (to measure with the instrument below)
Method: probe - grep of `^from playwright` / `from PIL` against `ls requirements*.txt pyproject.toml`; not built because both files are at the repo root, outside this context (veto 1)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rln '^from playwright' --include=*.py . -> 8 files; grep -rln 'from PIL' -> src/variants/subtle/tools/crop.py, src/variants/subtle/tools/grid.py; ls requirements*.txt pyproject.toml -> none; README.md:84 names python scripts/shots.py with no install step
instrument: node one-liner: collect third-party imports from `git ls-files '*.py'` and assert each appears in requirements-tools.txt (2 undeclared -> 0)

title: Legacy facet reader turns a missing security facet into 'PUBLIC' data and value 1
standard: repo law (docs/blueprint-ui.md: lenses are data; 'unmeasured' is a health of its own)
body:
## Summary
src/variants/base/legacy.ts fills absent facet fields with defaults that read as facts, so a feature with no facet shows 'PUBLIC' data, 'Value 1/5', 'NOT DEPLOYED' and so on in the shaped and bold variants.

## Description
bl() (src/variants/base/legacy.ts:41-70) defaults security.dataClass to 'public', business.value to 1, operations.environment to 'none', design.status to 'none', development.status to 'not-started', quality.status to 'n/a'. The shaped and bold channels print those as evidence (src/variants/shaped/channels.ts:240 CLASSW -> 'PUBLIC'; bold content 'value 1/5') and size shapes and fences by them. For a live product (`?product=`) whose scan has not produced a security facet, the plan says the feature handles only public data: the absence of a record is drawn as a reassuring measurement. Fixed = missing fields stay unknown (null / '') and the built-in channels render the lens as unmeasured, as the manifest-driven subtle channel already does (lensContent says NOT MEASURED).

## Flow
- feature with no facets -> bl(f) -> security.dataClass 'public' -> shaped content 'PUBLIC · NOT REVIEWED', no cut corner; bold no shield
- fix: legacy defaults to unknown; each shaped/bold channel's content and marks short-circuit on health 'unmeasured' to the shared NOT MEASURED wording

## Expected impact
Shaped and bold stop asserting facts for unmeasured lenses on live products. Could break: Kettle has every facet and renders unchanged; channel code that assumes a string needs guards (~12 sites across base, shaped, bold).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a missing facet renders as unmeasured, not as a value
Before: 10 of 31 non-health fields assert a value on a feature with no facet (probe: bl({lens:{}}))
After: 0 of 31 (to measure with the same probe, plus a content() census over the 12 shaped/bold built-in channels on a facet-less feature)
Method: probe - node with type stripping over src/variants/base/legacy.ts; the change spans base, shaped and bold (M, risk 4), so it is not landed unread
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: node type-stripping probe: bl({lens:{}}) field census (10 -> 0) plus content() over the 12 shaped/bold built-in channels on a facet-less feature, counting parts other than NOT MEASURED

title: No gate checks rail.css sizes against chrome.ts; a comment keeps them in step
body:
## Summary
The rail's CSS sizes (#rail width 64 + right 14, #flyout width 340) and the engine's layout constants (railWidth() = 86, FLYOUT_W = 340 in src/engine/chrome.ts) are two hand-maintained copies of one vocabulary; only a comment (src/components/rail.css:2-3) keeps them in step.

## Description
src/engine/chrome.ts:7-8 returns 86 for the rail's footprint (64 + 14 edge + 8 gap) and :14 exports FLYOUT_W = 340, which the engine uses for the plan's safe area and overlay clearance (Engine.ts:277-278, overlayRight). src/components/rail.css:8 sets #rail width 64px and right 14px, and :45 sets #flyout width 340px. This round moved #flyout right onto --rw (d9fe3c2), but the remaining three numbers still drift silently: change one side and every gate stays green while the home fit clips under the rail or plan overlays slide under the flyout. Fixed looks like: a node check that parses both files and fails on disagreement, wired as an npm gate (cross-language-token-parity: a parity checker that reads the definitions it compares).

## Flow
- build scripts/check-chrome-sizes.mjs: read chrome.ts (railWidth's shown return, FLYOUT_W) and rail.css (#rail width + right, #flyout width) with comment-stripped regexes
- assert 64 + 14 + 8 === railWidth() and #flyout width === FLYOUT_W; exit 1 with both figures on mismatch
- wire `check:chrome` in package.json and add it to the overlay's always-gates
- seed red: set #flyout width to 360px, watch it fail; restore, watch it pass

## Expected impact
A designer or agent resizing the rail or flyout gets a red gate instead of a plan that fits under chrome. Could break: nothing at runtime; a regex that stops matching after a CSS reformat must fail loud, not pass.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a drift between rail.css and chrome.ts is caught by a gate
Before: 0 of 5 package.json gates read rail.css or chrome.ts (grep scripts/ package.json); 3 literal pairs guarded by a comment
After: predicted 3 of 3 pairs checked, seeded mismatch red - not taken
Method: simulation - the instrument lives in scripts/ and package.json, outside this round's paths (package.json is director-owned)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: scripts/check-chrome-sizes.mjs + npm script check:chrome; seed #flyout width 340 -> 360 and assert exit 1, restore and assert exit 0
